questions.question: Off-ramps:

options.text: Should not be used by trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for trucks.
questions.explanation: Off-ramps can be dangerous for trucks. Speed limits posted for ramps are safe for cars but may be too fast for trucks.

questions.question: When traveling under 40 mph, you should maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length.
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add at least one more second.

questions.question: When driving:

options.text: It is best to hide your intentions from others.
You should only use turn signals if vehicles are near you.
You should not use turn signals in construction zones.
You should always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do by using signals. Signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer:

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Put a large, heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Never open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening doors gives the fire more air, which makes the fire bigger and more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should apply the brakes:

options.text: The same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
While putting the vehicle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a plan for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a problem?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking
questions.explanation: Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts. Parts must be properly mounted and not touch other vehicle parts.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps keep an engine working properly:
questions.correctAnswerText: In any weather.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Antifreeze helps your engine work well in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: If using a helper when backing a vehicle, the helper should stand:

options.text: In front of the passenger's side.
In front of the driver's side.
Near the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck.
questions.explanation: When backing up, use a helper to watch blind spots. The helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where the driver can see them.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Can be avoided by eating while driving.
Can be increased by pre-programming radio stations.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations with others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations with others.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with passengers), or both (texting on a phone). Avoid distractions by pre-programming your radio, planning your route, avoiding difficult conversations while driving, adjusting mirrors before you leave, and not eating, drinking, or smoking while driving.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Place emergency warning devices.
questions.explanation: You must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your vehicle's air tanks, the brakes:
questions.correctAnswerText: May not work correctly.
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil buildup. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can stop the brakes from working correctly.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.correctAnswerText: A brake drum.
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are located inside the brake drum.

questions.question: In extremely hot conditions, you may have to:

options.text: Increase your speed to cool the engine.
Reduce your speed to prevent overheating.
Follow other vehicles more closely than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to prevent overheating.
questions.explanation: Going faster makes the engine and tires hotter. Slow down in very hot weather to avoid the engine overheating.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: The brake pedal should be pressed down gradually.
The brake pedal should be pushed down quickly.
The brake pedal should be pressed down repeatedly, but not held down continuously.
The amount of force required on the brake pedal will be the same each time you slow or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake pedal should be pressed down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The brake pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Stop harder than you would in a vehicle not equipped with ABS.
Use extra braking force to ensure the ABS kicks in.
Brake as you would in a vehicle not equipped with ABS.
Brake with less force than you would in a vehicle not equipped with ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as you would in a vehicle not equipped with ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When driving in winter, which of the following needs extra attention during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: In winter, always check that the coolant and antifreeze are at safe levels.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Continue trying to get your vehicle off the tracks until you are successful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave it immediately and get away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts at the crossing and call 911.

questions.question: An air supply control in its "emergency" position will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.
